prs.title: fix(nitro): transform server auto-imports in `node_modules` layers
prs.author: maxirozay
prs.body: …_modules ### 🔗 Linked issue resolves #36811 ### 📚 Description Nuxt doesn't auto import layers server utils if they are in node_modules because `ServerAutoImportsPlugin` use a regex that exclude node_modules and git folders. The fix use the existing `getLayerNodeModulesExcludePattern` to feed `ServerAutoImportsPlugin` and have the `excludePattern` set only in one place.

prs.title: fix(nuxt): type island component props as json-serializable
prs.author: onmax
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description server components get their props through `JSON.stringify`, but the generated `IslandComponent` type accepts whatever the component declares. so passing a `Date`, a function, a `Map` and so on type-checks fine, and then on the server it arrives as a string or isn't there at all. this narrows the props of island components to values that survive serialization, recursing into objects and arrays. event handlers and vnode props (`key`, `ref`, …) keep their original types

prs.title: fix(nitro): stream the body read through a `nuxt/server` handler
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

### 📚 Description

previously, reading `event.req.body` as a stream in a `nuxt/server` handler didn't actually stream; the handler gets the whole upload back as a single chunk, and only once the client had finished sending it

this PR reads the body from the incoming request chunk by chunk, only as far as a reader has pulled it, and keeps the chunks so every later read still resolves the same bytes.

prs.title: fix(nuxt): replay lazy hydration interactions
prs.author: waleedtariq109
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue Resolves #36800 ### 📚 Description Fixes `hydrate-on-interaction` losing the event that triggers hydration. Nuxt wraps the lazy component in two async components. Previously, Vue replayed the triggering event after the outer wrapper hydrated, before the inner component had loaded and attached its listeners. Interactions are now queued during loading and replayed after the inner component mounts. Component loading remains deferred until interaction, and pending events are discarded when the component unmounts. Adds regression coverage for clicks, touch events, cached components, fragment roots, custom triggers, and unmount cleanup. Updates the existing end-to-end test to require the first click to increment. Validation: - Eight focused regression tests passed. - Real Chrome click and tap checks passed. - Focused TypeScript and diff checks passed. - The full Nuxt test suite was not run.

prs.title: feat(nitro): support nitro rspack builder
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description nitro `3.0.261103-rc` ships an experimental `rspack` builder, and it already works with nuxt when building with webpack or rspack: ```ts export default defineNuxtConfig({ builder: 'rspack', nitro: { builder: 'rspack' }, }) ``` this PR fixes the following warning: ``` [nitro] WARN The rspack builder ignores these rollupConfig / rolldownConfig options: tsconfig. Use rspackConfig instead. ``` ... and also passes the resolved `@rspack/core` version to nitro so nitro won't prompt to reinstall. (nitro should probably declare an optional peer dependency instead of requiring this, fwiw.)

prs.title: fix(nuxt): keep build cache file names longer than 100 bytes
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36810#pullrequestreview-5767516319 (cc: @onmax) ### 📚 Description on a build cache hit with `experimental.nitroViteEnvironment: false`, a long ssr chunk path breaks the nitro build: ```text [UNRESOLVED_IMPORT] Could not resolve './_nuxt/-.js' in .nuxt/dist/server/server.mjs ``` this is the same issue that https://github.com/unjs/nanotar/pull/74 fixes this PR swaps `nanotar` for `modern-tar`, which writes `pax` headers for longer names, and adds a cache format version to the build hash so caches written in the old format miss instead of restoring truncated files.

prs.title: perf(vite): list ssr-styles imports without deserializing the AST
prs.author: onmax
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

related rolldown/rolldown#11390

### 📚 Description

`ssr-styles` only needs a module's import specifiers, but `this.parse()` made rolldown serialize the whole AST to JSON and rebuild it in JS.

this reads `module.staticImports` from `parseSync` instead, so the AST is never rebuilt.

prs.title: perf(nuxt): look up component names by file path
prs.author: onmax
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description `nuxt:component-name-plugin` ran `getComponents().find()` for every vue and jsx module, so each transform walked the whole components list, which adds up in apps with thousands of components. this looks components up in a map by file path instead, rebuilt when the components array changes.

prs.title: fix(nuxt): preserve the types of multiple async data addons
prs.author: DamianGlowala
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue spotted locally while trying to add multiple addons ### 📚 Description When several addons are passed to `createUseAsyncData` or `createUseFetch`, one addon can erase the types of the others. For example, an addon that adds an extension, combined with one that adds nothing, gives a composable with no extension in its types. Everything still works at runtime, so the code runs fine but won't typecheck.

prs.title: perf(nuxt,nitro): reuse the restored ssr build on build cache hits
prs.author: onmax
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

no issue. reproduction on main: https://github.com/onmax/repros/tree/repro/nuxt-build-cache-ssr-rebuild/nuxt-build-cache-ssr-rebuild (`pnpm verify` builds twice, and ssr builds again on the cache hit)

### 📚 Description

with `experimental.buildCache`, a cache hit restores the client and ssr output, but nitro still builds the ssr environment again, which takes about 4.4s in prod. skipping it outright isn't safe, because the cache key leaves out the nitro options and virtual modules the ssr build reads. for example, `NITRO_PRESET=cloudflare-module nuxt build` after a `node-server` build gives the same key, and a plain skip would ship ssr code resolved for node inside a worker.

this writes a `nuxt-ssr-inputs.json` fingerprint next to the ssr output. it holds a hash of each output file, of the ssr environment's `define`, `resolve` and `build` options, and of each nitro virtual module the build bundled. on a cache hit, the server builder checks the fingerprint through a new optional `canReuseSsrBuild` on `NuxtServerBuild`. it marks ssr as built only when every hash matches, and otherwise ssr builds as it does today.

the reuse also needs the tar to keep every file name. nanotar's `createTar` cuts names to 100 bytes (unjs/nanotar#29), and ssr chunk paths can be longer, for example `vite/services/ssr/_nuxt/<long component name>-<hash>.js`. the restore then writes that file under the wrong name, the fingerprint check finds it missing, and ssr builds again on e
…(truncated)

prs.title: fix(vite): resolve bare imports from component wrappers
prs.author: benjamincanac
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description Noticed this while testing #36671 on a pnpm project that doesn't list `vue` as a direct dependency. Any lazy component fails the build, and the page 500s in dev: ``` Error: [vite]: Rolldown failed to resolve import "vue" from "\0/virtual:nuxt-component:lazy:Foo:QfyRsBdcHG:...". ``` The component wrappers from #36763 resolve to `\0/virtual:nuxt-component:*`, which `nuxt:resolve-bare-imports` didn't recognise as a virtual importer, so `vue` fell through to Vite resolving it from the project root. This PR lets that importer through so it resolves from the app dir like the other virtual modules. Changing the wrapper ids to `\0virtual:nuxt-component:*` would also work if you'd rather fix it on that side.

prs.title: fix(vite): externalize ssr deps the same way regardless of import order
prs.author: onmax
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

resolves #36795

### 📚 Description

`ufo` ended up in different chunks depending on load order. `#internal/nuxt/paths` imports it by absolute path, which `nuxt:resolve-externals` didn't match, so it was bundled, while imports by name were externalized. rolldown keeps whichever resolution it sees first (rolldown/rolldown#11417).

this also externalizes an absolute import of a package entry when its bare import is external, so both resolve the same way.

prs.title: fix(vite): don't add css links if only shared with spa pages
prs.author: aaronanish-t
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue Resolves #36741 ### 📚 Description With `inlineStyles` enabled, pages that share a CSS file with an `ssr: false` page still get a render-blocking `` for that CSS, even though it's already inlined in the HTML. Nuxt only drops the link when every importer of the CSS ends at a component that inlined it (`isInlinedForEveryImporter` in `ssr-styles.ts`). The `ssr: false` page is never server-rendered, so it never inlines anything. The check reaches it, gives up, and keeps the link on every page. This PR exposes the existing `spaOnly` pages as `_spaOnlyPageSources`, the same way `_noScriptsPageSources` is exposed, and treats them as satisfied in the importer check. This is safe because an `ssr: false` page only ever runs in the browser, and Vite loads its CSS with its JS chunk. I served the generated fixture and opened its `ssr: false` page directly; it still loads `spa-shared.css` and the style applies. I added two pages to the `inline-styles` fixture (one normal, one `ssr: false`, sharing one CSS file) and a case to `test/inline-styles.test.ts`. It fails without the fix (the extra `` is present) and passes with it. I've only changed the Vite plugin. The webpack plugin drops links differently, in a `build:manifest` hook with no importer walk, so I don't think it's affected. I haven't tested it, though.

prs.title: fix(vite): fall back to node source maps for stack frames outside `vite-node`
prs.author: atinux
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue Following #33989 and #36258 ### 📚 Description Nuxt's dev server replaced Node's stack-trace formatter, so errors from files Nuxt didn't load itself pointed at the generated code instead of the source. The fix makes Nuxt fallback to Node's own source map, so the stack points back at the original source again.

prs.title: feat(kit,nitro,nuxt,rspack,schema,webpack): add rsbuild builder
prs.author: Nsttt
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

Follow-up to #35489, which moved `@nuxt/rspack-builder` onto Rsbuild and kept `rspack` as the public builder name.

### 📚 Description

This adds a new builder package, `@nuxt/rsbuild-builder`, enabled with `builder: 'rsbuild'`. It also deprecates `@nuxt/rspack-builder`.

The rspack builder runs on Rsbuild today, but Rsbuild only drives the dev server and the compiler lifecycle there. The Rspack configuration still comes from the webpack presets, with loaders for CSS, PostCSS, esbuild and assets. The new builder hands the build to Rsbuild itself:

- `client` and `server` are Rsbuild environments.
- Rsbuild options cover entries, defines, aliases, output paths and filenames, source maps, externals, decorators and JSX through SWC, CSS through Lightning CSS and PostCSS, chunk splitting, the dev server and HMR.
- Vue goes through `@rsbuild/plugin-vue`.
- Nuxt's own logic lives in Rsbuild plugins that use `processAssets`, `transform`, `modifyBundlerChain` and the environment compile hooks.

A few things have no Rsbuild option, so they still use Rspack configuration:

- Resolving packages and loaders from Nuxt's `modulesDir`.
- The Node.js polyfills of `experimental.clientNodeCompat`.
- The SSR styles plugin, which is shared with the webpack builder.
- Bundle analysis with `webpack-bundle-analyzer`.

In dev, the Rsbuild dev server runs in middleware mode behind the Nuxt dev server, and the HMR socket shares its port, like the rspack builder.

#### Compatibility

prs.title: fix(nuxt): resolve wildcard redirect targets in the route rules matcher
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description with a wildcard redirect rule like this: ```ts export default defineNuxtConfig({ routeRules: { '/old/**': { redirect: '/new/**' }, }, }) ``` a server request for `/old/a/b` redirects to `/new/a/b`, but navigating to `/old/a/b` on the client (or calling `getRouteRules({ path: '/old/a/b' })`) gives `/new/**` literally. this PR keeps `{ to, base }` for wildcard redirects in the matcher and moves the tail onto the target there, following what nitro does on the server

prs.title: fix(nuxt): keep app manifest requests alive during page unload
prs.author: lafllamme
prs.body: Fixes #36835. WebKit can cancel an app manifest request when leaving the page, which causes Nuxt to log E5002. This adds `keepalive` to let the request finish during page unload. Genuine fetch errors are still reported. I initially tried aborting the request on `beforeunload`. That removed E5002, but cancelling navigation could leave the update checker with an unhandled rejection. Using `keepalive` avoids interrupting the request and needs no lifecycle listeners. Validation: - 47 focused tests passed, including six manifest tests. Removing `keepalive` makes the regression test fail. - Typecheck, lint, both Knip checks and all 12 bundle tests passed locally. - A small production Nuxt app in WebKit logged E5002 before the fix and no E5002 after it. Cancelling navigation also left the update checker running without errors. - A Firefox harness running the manifest source restored the same document from the back/forward cache with the fix. The WebKit checks used Playwright 1.55.0 / WebKit 2203. The Firefox check used Playwright 1.64.1 / Firefox 157. The full test matrix and mobile Safari were not tested. The bundle snapshot changes were generated by Nuxt's `autofix.ci` workflow. I kept them after verifying that the bundle tests pass on the updated branch; the manifest fix does not manually change server bundling.

prs.title: fix(nitro): dispatch compat `$fetch` to the current dev app
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description with v2 compat + nitro vite environment, after you edit a server route, SSR useFetch / $fetch keeps getting the old handler's response. this imports fetch from nitro instead, which already handles looking up the current app through `globalThis.__nitro__`

prs.title: fix(schema): detect git worktrees and submodules as workspace roots
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description since 4.6.4, `workspaceDir` only widens past `rootDir` to a declared workspace root or the closest git repository. but we only detect a repository by its `.git/config`, and in a git worktree or submodule `.git` can be a file. so this also treats a `.git` file starting with `gitdir:` as a repository root.

prs.title: fix(vite): apply browser global defines in dev ssr
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description noticed when upgrading nuxt.com to the v5 nightly, that `ProseImg` rendered nothing in dev SSR, and every blog image gave a hydration mismatch. so this PR applies window defines in dev too (I think the onPrehydrate bug I encountered before is now gone) and this also fixes an issue where user `vite.environments` were being overwritten by $server/$client options

prs.title: fix(nitro): report and type a direct h3 v1 dependency
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description spotted this when upgrading nuxt.com to the Nuxt 5 nightly. nuxt.com has a direct `h3` v1 dependency, and with `nitroLegacy` off no Nuxt diagnostic appeared, but things just failed at runtime this is because nothing redirects `h3` for user code unless `nitroLegacy.h3` is on this PR adds `NUXT_B9009`, which lists user server files with a value import from `h3` when the project resolves `h3` to v1, unless `nitroLegacy.h3` is on: ``` WARN [NUXT_B9009] 2 files in your server code import from h3, which your project resolves to h3@1.15.11. Nitro v3 uses h3 v2, and h3 v1 helpers do not work with its events: - server/api/cookie.ts - server/api/hello.ts ╰▶ fix: Remove h3 from your dependencies and import from nuxt/server (or nitro/h3) instead. To ship before migrating, enable nitroLegacy.h3, which resolves h3 to the h3 v1 helpers. ``` I've also updated the upgrade guide

prs.title: perf(vite): ensure static imports needed by entry are bundled with it
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

### 📚 Description

another from benchmarking a Nuxt UI marketing page (~690 components). the JS it requests up front was spread over a lot of small chunks:

| initial JS for `/` (`ui` bench fixture) | files | gzip |
| - | - | - |
| main | 18 | 175.3 kB |
| + entry group | 10 | 170.4 kB |
| + layout group | 6 | 167.0 kB |

there are two reasons:

1. in some apps (this one included) rolldown keeps modules shared by the entry and lazy chunks (vue, for example) in common chunks of their own, even though they're always loaded with the entry.
2. the dependencies of a layout get split into one common chunk per set of pages that also use them, even though the layout is always on the critical path.

so this PR does two things:

- we ensure that modules tagged `$initial` are in the entry chunk
-  when the app has exactly one layout, the static dependencies of that layout share one chunk. this is a narrow optimisation because I didn't want to inadvertently introduce a perf regression - and note that this one can be turned off with `experimental.layoutChunk: false`

both are skipped in dev, when the client build has more than one entry, and when `codeSplitting`, `manualChunks`, `advancedChunks` or `inlineDynamicImports` is already set.

the trade-off is mostly caching. vue and the other initial dependencies now live in the entry chunk, so any change to the initial graph means downloading all of it again, not just the app code.

having said that, I think it's worth i
…(truncated)

prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description this addressses some issues found when upgrading nuxt.com/npmx.dev/roe.dev to nuxt v5 1. Nitro v3 cached handlers drop the query unless `allowQuery` is set, so island requests lost their props query 2. `Nitro config hot reloaded` printed on every start/build 3. provide better errors for route rules like `/api/content/pull/*/*/blob/**` which nitro now disallows

prs.title: feat(nuxt): add `experimental.staticRoutes` for greater perf
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue follow-on from https://github.com/vuejs/router/pull/2804 https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36728 🫡 https://github.com/nuxt-modules/i18n/pull/4184 cc: @onmax ### 📚 Description currently - and by default - a fresh `Router` is created for every SSR request, and `createRouter` rebuilds the vue-router matcher from `routes` each time. on the bench `large` fixture this is about half of a small page's render time. this PR adds an `experimental.staticRoutes` option. on the server - if enabled: - the server builds one matcher per `routes` array and passes it to every request's `createRouter` - `early404` is enabled, unless a layer sets it to `false` explicitly - `router.addRoute`, `removeRoute` and `clearRoutes` throw (`NUXT_E2014`) and are removed from the `useRouter` type, through the augmentation `early404` already uses - a `router.options` file that modifies `routes` fails the build (`NUXT_B4027`) rather than silently losing the optimisations | `large` fixture, 8 connections | `main` | this PR | | --- | --- | --- | | `/` | 1324 req/s | 2700 req/s (+104%) | | `/catalog/3` | 1411 req/s | 2932 req/s (+108%) | | `/table` (1000 `` rows) | 247 req/s | 292 req/s (+18%) | | `/table/plain` | 322 req/s | 386 req/s (+20%) |

prs.title: fix(nuxt): reload when navigating to a payload from another build
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue resolves #33666 ### 📚 Description after a deploy, a client that is still running the previous build will fetch `/foo/_payload.json?_b=` on navigation and get the payload rendered by the new build. this PR adds the `buildId` to the extracted `_payload.json`, and the client now checks it against its own build: | when | what happens | | --- | --- | | navigating | the payload is discarded and we reload at the destination (as with chunk errors) | | prefetching | the payload is discarded and `app:manifest:update` is called once, so `emitRouteChunkError` handling and any 'new version' UI kicks in | | `loadPayload()` | returns `null` |

prs.title: fix(nuxt): process templates individually when debugging
prs.author: onmax
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description templates compile concurrently, so a single slow template pushed every other pending template over the 500ms threshold and we'd log a `Compiled …` line for each one, blaming templates that did almost nothing. this logs a single line for the whole run instead, suggesting `debug: { templates: true }`. with that enabled, each template now reports both how long its own code ran and its elapsed time.

prs.title: fix(nuxt): skip navigation repaint during view transition updates
prs.author: waleedtariq109
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue Resolves #36768 ### 📚 Description With view transitions enabled, the navigation repaint guard waits for an animation frame while rendering is paused by the transition’s update callback. This causes navigation to wait for the 100 ms fallback timeout. This change skips the repaint wait while a view-transition update is pending. Normal repaint behavior resumes when the update completes or fails. Cleanup also checks transition identity so an older transition cannot clear a newer transition’s state. Regression tests cover active transitions, disabled transitions, reduced-motion preferences, unsupported browsers, successful and failed updates, and overlapping transitions. Validation: - Regression tests fail without the fix. - All 15 focused tests pass with the fix. - Lint and whitespace checks pass.

prs.title: fix(vite): bundle Vue dependencies to avoid absolute SSR paths
prs.author: waleedtariq109
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

Resolves #36776

### 📚 Description

Disable the `require()` polyfill in intermediate Vite SSR output so the final server builder can resolve dependencies without retaining absolute build-time paths. Keep the polyfill enabled for combined builds.

This preserves existing dependency externalization and avoids creating separate Vue runtimes for the app and external libraries.

Regression tests cover external Vue consumers, dynamic imports, runtime compilation, and build-time paths across emitted JavaScript files.

Validated with 28 passing tests, lint, and five isolated production smoke tests. Additional Rollup validation encountered output issues also present on the baseline.

prs.title: fix(nuxt): watch `shared/` for auto-import changes
prs.author: onmax
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue no issue. repro: https://github.com/onmax/repros/tree/repro/nuxt-stale-auto-imports-after-stash ### 📚 Description when files in `shared/` change on disk without going through the editor (e.g. `git stash`), nuxt doesn't pick it up. auto-imports from `shared/utils` and `shared/types` keep pointing at the old exports until you restart the dev server. this adds the `shared/` directory to the watched paths, so adding, removing or stashing files there regenerates the auto-imports the same way it already does for `app/` and `server/`.
